title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: notes on the moduli of elliptic curves in residue characteristics ≠ 2 (cote 64). Grothendieck studies faithful actions of the Klein four-group V ≅ F2×F2 (he writes it 𝔻_4, the dihedral group of order 4) on a relative P^1, X/S. The previous page normalises such an action étale-locally. Let σ1 be an involution with fixed-point divisor Δ1. Locally (X, Δ1) ≅ (P^1_S, {0,∞}) and σ1(z) = −z. A second commuting involution σ2 must swap 0 and ∞, and its fixed points form an étale divisor Δ2 stable under σ1. After extracting a square root étale-locally and rescaling z, one gets Δ2 = {1,−1} and σ2(z) = 1/z; this is normal form (4).

This page computes the third involution σ3 = σ1σ2: z ↦ −1/z. Its fixed-point divisor is Δ3 = V(z^2+1). This is étale because 2 is invertible on S. It splits as {i,−i} when S has a primitive 4th root of unity.

Proposition: étale-locally on S (residue characteristics ≠ 2), every fibrewise-faithful representation of V in Aut(P^1_S) is conjugate to (4). Conversely, (4) does give a faithful representation.

Definition (6): Δ = Δ1 ⊔ Δ2 ⊔ Δ3, the disjoint union of the fixed-point divisors of the three non-trivial elements. In the normalised case Δ = {0,∞,±1,±i}, the six vertices of the regular octahedron on the Riemann sphere. Δ is called the octahedral configuration attached to the action. It is a finite étale divisor of degree 6 of X/S. The definition also works for a twisted form V̲, i.e. a group scheme étale-locally isomorphic to the constant V.

General definition: an octahedral configuration in X/S is a degree-6 étale divisor étale-locally isomorphic to {0,∞,±1,±i} ⊂ P^1_S. The next page shows that the action is essentially unique: Aut_S(X,Δ) is finite étale and locally ≅ (𝔖_4)_S, the rotation group of a combinatorial octahedron structure on Δ.

Purpose: this is a relative, étale-local version of the classical fact that Klein four-subgroups of PGL2 (char ≠ 2) are all conjugate, with normaliser 𝔖_4 (the octahedral group). In the elliptic-curve setting, V presumably arises from translations by 2-torsion acting on the quotient P^1 = E/±1, which preserve the 4 branch points. This is a tool for describing level-2 / Legendre-type structures on the moduli of elliptic curves over Z[1/2].
errors: No mathematical error. σ3 = σ1σ2 = −1/z is correct, and its fixed points are the roots of z^2+1. The divisor is étale since disc = −4 is invertible.
Implicit hypothesis: the action must be faithful on every fibre (Grothendieck adds this in an insertion). This is needed so that each σ_j has an étale fixed divisor of degree 2 everywhere.
Notation 𝔻_4 for the Klein four-group (dihedral group of order 4) is idiosyncratic but not wrong.

ideas.what: Étale-local normal form of a faithful Klein-four action on P^1_S over Z[1/2]: σ1 = −z, σ2 = 1/z, σ3 = −1/z
ideas.modern_name: Klein four-subgroups of PGL2 are a single conjugacy class (relative/étale-local version)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Klein, Vorlesungen über das Ikosaeder, 1884); relative version folklore

ideas.what: Octahedral configuration: the degree-6 étale divisor formed by the union of the fixed points of the three involutions, locally {0,∞,±1,±i}
ideas.modern_name: Octahedral point configuration / orbit of the octahedral group on P^1; twisted forms classified by H^1(S, 𝔖_4)

ideas.what: Allowing a twisted group scheme V̲ (étale-locally constant) instead of the constant group
ideas.modern_name: Forms of finite étale group schemes, torsors and descent

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful relativisation over Z[1/2] of Klein's classical octahedral configuration and of the conjugacy of Klein four-subgroups of PGL2. It is standard material serving the elliptic-curve moduli project; nothing here appears absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: In (5) the marginal note reads 'si ∃ racine primitive 4e de 1 sur S' (a primitive 4th root of unity), not 'de ξ−1'.
'les autres correspondant' should read 'les automorphismes correspondant' (σ1, σ2 are the automorphisms attached to e1, e2).

The garbled passage around 'à l'opération de V sur X' reads roughly: 'associée à l'opération de V sur X (par descente, comme diviseur étale plat, elle est définie comme diviseur étale de degré 6 de X/S) dès qu'on a une opération monomorphique (sur chaque fibre) d'un groupe V ≃ 𝔻_4 sur X'. The transcription duplicates phrases here.
The top '2' is a page/section marker continuing the equation numbering. Equation (5) gives σ3(z) = −1/z, not '=' with a stray sign.
